docs.title: ITS Ontology - Traffic Regulation Topic Area
docs.text:
This ontology imports the Traffic Regulation topic area modules (core, patterns, and constraints).

License: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

The ITS Ontology - Traffic Regulation Topic Area consists of the following patterns:

  • Condition
  • Core
  • Enforcement
  • Permit
  • Traffic Control Device
  • Traffic Regulation

The formal definition of this ontology is available in TURTLE Syntax.

docs.title: Condition
docs.text:
A boolean condition that must evaluate to true for the associated regulation(s) to currently apply. Even if the condition is true, it is not active if it is currently overridden. The condition may be multi-part.

IRI: https://w3id.org/itsdata/regulation/v1/Condition

docs.title: Specializations of Condition
docs.text: Class Description Condition Set A composite condition that consists of two or more Conditions combined by a logical operator; the set must evaluate to true for the associated regulation(s) to currently apply. Enumerated Condition A condition that is based on an enumerated value in a known code list. Location Condition A condition that applies to a specific location. Measurable Condition A condition that is based on a comparison between a measurable value and a threshold value. Permit Required Condition A condition that is based on the possession of a permit. Time Validity Condition A condition that applies to a specific location. Versioned Condition A specific version of a condition that can be referenced by a ConditionReference.

docs.text: Class Description Access Category Code A code that indicates categories of access to a location that can affect the applicability of a regulation. Goods Type Code<sup>1</sup> A code that indicates the type of goods (especially hazardous goods) that is carried by a vehicle. Load Type Code<sup>1</sup> A code that indicates categories of load types that can affect the applicability of a regulation. Road Type Code A code that indicates categories of roads that can affect the applicability of a regulation. Road Weather Condition Code<sup>1</sup> Standing Or Parking Category Code A code that indicates categories of standing or parking that can affect the applicability of a regulation. Tunnel Category Code A code that indicates categories of tunnels that can affect the applicability of a regulation. Vehicle Equipment Code<sup>1</sup> A code that indicates the type of equipment that is carried by a vehicle. Vehicle Type Code<sup>1</sup> A code that indicates the type of vehicle. Vehicle Usage Code<sup>1</sup> A code that indicates the usage of a vehicle.

docs.title: Traffic Regulation Ontology
docs.text:
This ontology defines concepts related to traffic regulations.

This pattern imports the following files:

  • https://w3id.org/citydata/part1/v1/
  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/agent/v1/
  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/location/v1/
  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/regulation/v1/CorePattern
  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/regulation/v1/PermitPattern
  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/t-user/v1/
  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/time/v1/

This pattern consists of the following classes:

  • Access Category Code
  • Condition
  • Condition Code
  • Condition Set
  • Driver Category Code
  • Enumerated Condition
  • Legal Basis
  • Legal Status Code
  • Location Condition
  • Logical Operator Code
  • Measurable Condition
  • Measurable Condition Code
  • Permit Required Condition
  • Road Type Code
  • Standing Or Parking Category Code
  • Time Validity Condition
  • Tunnel Category Code
  • Versioned Condition

This module defines the following properties:

  • applicableLocation
  • comparisonOperator
  • forAccessCategory
  • forEnumeratedCondition
  • forMeasurableCondition
  • forNonVehicularRoadUserType
  • forRoadType
  • forRoadWeatherConditionType
  • forStandingOrParkingCategory
  • forTunnelCategory
  • hasCondition
  • hasLegalBasis
  • implementedLocation
  • implementedValidity
  • isActive
  • locationByOrder
  • logicalOperator
  • negate
  • otherCondition
  • requiredDesignation
  • requiredDisplayType
  • requiredGrantor
  • requiredGrantorType
  • requiredPermitIdentifier
  • trafficImpactLocation
  • validityByOrder
  • valueToCompare
  • version

The formal definition of this pattern is available in TURTLE Syntax in two files, the core semantics and the SHACL restrictions.

Immobilization Enforcement Method A method of enforcing a traffic regulation that involves immobilizing a vehicle. Towing Enforcement Method A method of enforcing a traffic regulation that involves towing a vehicle.

docs.title: The Traffic Regulation Pattern of the Traffic Regulation Ontology
docs.text:
This ontology defines concepts related to traffic regulations.

This pattern imports the following files:

  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/regulation/v1/ConditionPattern
  • https://w3id.org/itsdata/regulation/v1/CorePattern

This pattern consists of the following classes:

  • Activation Status Code
  • Coded Pair Regulation
  • Coded Regulation
  • Coded Regulation With Fee
  • Coded Regulation With Threshold
  • Fee Restriction Code
  • Reason Code
  • Regulation Category Code
  • Regulation Category Code List
  • Regulation Context Code
  • Regulatory Scope Code
  • Required Supplemental Data
  • Restriction Code
  • Rule Maker Role
  • Stand Alone Restriction Code
  • Supplemental Data Type Code
  • Suspect Status Code
  • Textual Regulation
  • Threshold Restriction Code
  • Traffic Regulation
  • Traffic Regulation Order
  • Tro Status Code
  • Trustworthiness
  • Trustworthiness Code

This module defines the following properties:

  • associatedTrafficControlDevice
  • authorizingTrafficRegulation
  • hasActivationStatus
  • hasAssociatedRestriction
  • hasContext
  • hasFeeSchedule
  • hasInceptionDate
  • hasOverallTrustworthiness
  • hasPermitType
  • hasRegulationCategory
  • hasRestriction
  • hasTerminationDate
  • hasTextualRestriction
  • hasThreshold
  • hasTrustworthiness
  • issuedTro
  • isSuspect
  • memberTrafficRegulation
  • reasonCode
  • regulatoryScope
  • troStatus

The formal definition of this pattern is available in TURTLE Syntax in two files, the core semantics and the SHACL restrictions.
